description: Inventory, equipment-slot, meso and shop-behaviour rules that MeowDB MS Classic does not publish. Read by scripts/core/items/items_config.gd. Canonical item facts (tab, stack size, stats, requirements, prices) stay in data/canonical/items; this file only fills the gaps. See docs/runtime/ITEMS.md.
tab_slots_reason: MeowDB publishes no inventory size. The only canonical statement is Roger's line (npcs/3.json, formulas/loot_rules.json inventory_full): 'When your Item Inventory is full, you won't be able to pick up new items.' 24 slots per tab is the commonly remembered pre-Big-Bang starting size; it is NOT from MeowDB and is unverified. The value is a per-character default: the Inventory stores its own capacity in the save, so future slot expansions are save state.
equipment_max_stack_reason: MeowDB has no 'Max per Stack' row for any Equip item (items.md Gaps; max_stack is null on all 55 equips). Equipment is unstackable: one piece per slot, so each piece can carry per-instance data (future scroll results, stat rolls).
unpublished_max_stack_reason: Fallback for a non-equipment item whose canonical max_stack is null. No item in the current set hits this (every Use/Etc/Setup item has a value); 1 is the conservative choice so an unknown item can never overfill a slot.
meso_cap_reason: MeowDB documents no meso cap. 2,147,483,647 is the signed 32-bit limit of a classic meso counter (not from MeowDB, unverified); it exists so mesos can never overflow. Picking up or earning past it adds only up to the cap; a sale that would pass it is refused.
equipment_slots_reason: The first ten are the slots the brief names; canonical items use them through their derived equip_slot (items.md 'Derived fields'). The rest are the remaining classic equipment slots, present so future content is data only. No Maple Island item uses them yet.
slot_aliases_reason: A canonical equip_slot that maps to several equipment slots. Equipping picks the first empty one, else replaces the first. Unused on Maple Island (no rings in the item set).

slot_conflicts.reason: An overall covers both the top and the bottom.
A top cannot be worn over an overall.
A bottom cannot be worn with an overall.
A two-handed weapon leaves no hand for a shield.
A shield needs the off hand, so it unequips a two-handed weapon (a one-handed weapon stays).

slot_conflicts_reason: MeowDB item pages do not state slot conflicts. These are the classic rules, unverified. Equipping into 'slot' unequips the items in 'removes' into the inventory. 'if_two_handed' limits the rule to a two-handed incoming item; 'only_two_handed_occupant' removes the occupant only when it is two-handed.
weapon_subtypes_reason: Keys are MeowDB weapon subtypes (item 'subtype' / weapon.weapon_type). damage_family, multiplier_key and action_odds_key are the key names of formulas/damage.json physical.weapon_families, physical.weapon_action_multipliers and physical.ordinary_action_odds, read off MeowDB's own labels ('Sword / Axe / Blunt / Spear / Polearm', '1H Axe / Blunt', ...). two_handed is an adaptation: items.md Gaps says two-handedness is only implied by subtype names and MeowDB does not say whether Bow / Spear / Wand block a shield. Subtypes named Two-Handed are two-handed by name; Spear, Polearm, Bow, Crossbow and Claw follow the classic client convention (unverified); Wand and Staff are one-handed (unverified).
job_item_tags_reason: Which item 'requirements.job' strings a class slug satisfies. Transcribed from MeowDB's character builder (formulas/beginner.json equipment_restrictions.character_builder_code: h={beginner:[],warrior:["Warrior"],magician:["Mage"],bowman:["Bowman"],thief:["Thief"]}); a Beginner matches only items with no job requirement. 'pirate' is not in that code and is a guess for later iterations (unverified).

shop.sell_zero_value_items_reason: MeowDB records sell-back 0 for 25 items (all of Pan's stock, Sid's Sword/Hand Axe/Wooden Club, arrows, Roger's Apple, several quest items) but does not say whether an NPC refuses them or pays 0 (shops.md Gaps). MisoStory lets the NPC take them for 0 mesos so the shop doubles as a way to get rid of items (Roger: 'get rid of unimportant items by either discarding them or selling them at a store').
shop.max_bundles_per_purchase_reason: MeowDB documents no per-purchase limit (shops.md: quantity_per_purchase is not a limit). null = no limit beyond mesos and inventory space; the UI may clamp its quantity box.
